general_information.Description: Students develop and apply critical reading skills through the analysis of texts taken from authentic sources (journals, newspapers, magazines and websites) and a variety of academic disciplines. Students are encouraged to develop their comprehension, while at the same time forming a reasoned assessment of the effectiveness and validity of the text.
general_information.StudentTasks: "- Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfil tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes
general_information.Tools: Tools: Foxit pdf editor Internet access
general_information.Note: 1) On-going assessment - Assignments: 04*15%: 60% 2) Final Examination (FE) 40% 3) Final Result 100% 4) Completion Criteria: - On-going assessment >0, Final Exam Score >=4/10 & Final Result >=5/10 - If FE < 4/10, student must take resit exam (all parts);

description: Students develop and apply critical reading skills through the analysis of texts taken from authentic sources (journals, newspapers, magazines and websites) and a variety of academic disciplines. Students are encouraged to develop their comprehension, while at the same time forming a reasoned assessment of the effectiveness and validity of the text.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Use different reading strategies for different tasks, identify what critical reading is (and what it is not); understand the importance of critical reading skill; make questions and find answers as you read critically; differentiate between critical reading and other reading strategies; Develop and integrate criticality into reading practices.

Evaluate whether or not a text is academic; describe the peer-review process works; evaluate why peer-reviewed texts are preferable for academic study; understand the importance of the publication date of a text
Analyze the importance of knowing something about the author of a text and the people quoted by the author; recognize and reason bias
Identify the author’s stance; how the author’s intended audience influences the text; why the author’s purpose is important
Evaluate conclusions drawn from author experience; recognize the steps of the scientific method; evaluate important information as reading reports of empirical research

Identify and evaluate evidence not based on author experience: anecdotes, visual items, statistics and quotations from others; how authors try to persuade readers using no evidence at all; how to evaluate these kinds of evidence

Analyze the importance of considering the text in its broader context; recognize a school of thought and understand the importance of knowing the schools of thought in your area of study; how to approach a text that presents an opinion or theory very different from anything else you have read
Explain why it is important to ask yourself whether the text supports your own experiences; why it can be difficult to do this
Analyze the key components of a critical review; differentiate between a critical review and a research essay; structure a critical review

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ1.1
constructive_questions.Details: "Don’t believe in everything you read on the internet just because there's a picture with a quote next to it" (Abraham Lincoln). To what extent do you agree or disagree with that saying? Explain and provide examples from your own reading experience.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: What do you understand by the word "myth"? Do an Internet search about well-known myths from around the world or in Vietnam and share the myth that you are most interested in with your team. Imagine you are reading an article that tells you that the myth you have talked to your team is actually true. Do you believe it? What questions might you ask about the article?

constructive_questions.Details: How do you understand the term "critical reading" based on what you have learned in the lecture and from your own reading experience?

Share what you've known to your team. Can you think of any other creatures whose existence is uncertain? The reading is about a strange creature that is said to live in the waters of a lake north of Toronto, Ontario. Name six things you'd like to find out.

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ1.3
constructive_questions.Details: Have you known/heard about a mysterious creature in your culture? If yes, to what extent do you believe in the existence of that creature? Explain

constructive_questions.Details: Reading 3: after reading Discuss questions 1-6 (pp. 95-96)

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ9.1
constructive_questions.Details: What do you consider to be the top 10 characteristics of a great leader? Provide examples of exceptional international leaders to support your choices.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ25
constructive_questions.Details: What do you think are the essential skills needed to succeed in the business world? Think of some people who have been very successful in the business world (for example, Bill Gates, Steve Jobs and Mark Zuckerberg). What personal qualities do you associate them with? Do an Internet search for members of minority groups who have risen to leadership positions in their countries. How does society benefit from having diversity among its leaders?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ9.2
constructive_questions.Details: How would you distinguish between a leader and a manager? Use facts and examples from the reading and/or your own experience to support your response.

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ9.3
constructive_questions.Details: Would you prefer to work for an introvert or an extrovert leader? Explain your choice

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ27
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 2: before reading What is the difference between an introvert and an extrovert? Can you think of any leaders who are introverts or extroverts? Why do you think the writer might think we need quiet, introverted leaders? What advantages might introverts have over extrovert in leadership roles?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ10.1
constructive_questions.Details: Why have historically there been more prominent male leaders than female leaders? Include facts and examples from the reading and/or your own understanding to support your answer.

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ10.2

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ29
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 3: before reading What special characteristics can women bring to leadership roles in companies and other organizations? What challenges might women face in pursuing leadership roles? Which professions do you think might be underpresented by women in leadership roles? Why might this be the case?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ10.3
constructive_questions.Details: Mary Slaughter recommends women not to switch occupations too frequently, but also not to remain in the same position for too long. What do you think of her recommendation? Provide explanation and relevant examples to support your answers.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ30
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 3: after reading Discuss questions 1-8 (pp. 119-120)

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ11.1
constructive_questions.Details: What are the benefits and drawbacks of employing technology in education?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ31
constructive_questions.Details: How has education changed since the arrival of the computer era? Do you think PowerPoint is useful for students who want to understand the lectures well? Why or why not? You are going to read an article titled "Swimming againt the Tide of PowerPoint". What is 'tide'? What do you think the title of this reading mean? How have your educational experiences been different from those of your parentss' generation? What are advantages and disadvantages of using computer technology in education?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ11.2
constructive_questions.Details: To what extent do you agree or disagree with the author's assertion that he enjoys improvising during his lectures?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ32
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 1: After reading Do you think the author's reason for eschewing PowerPoint are good one? Why? What do you imagine the author's student might think about his teaching style? Which students might welcome his approach? Which students might disagree with it? How do you respond to the author's statement that he likes to improvide in his lecturers? Is improvision a useful technique in education? Would you like to take a course with thi kind of profesor? Why or why not?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ11.3
constructive_questions.Details: Do you believe mobile devices facilitate student learning? Explain your answers and provide relevant examples from your knowledge and experience.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ33
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 2: Before reading Do you own a laptop, smartphone or tablet? If so, have you ever used it for educational purposes? What was the result? Do you think mobile devices help student to learn? If so, which students benefit the most? If not, why not? Which do you prefer - learning with a mobile device or learning with a traditional book? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ12.1
constructive_questions.Details: After finishing the Reading 2, do you think that the number of participants in this study is sufficient enough for providing reliable data? Explain your answers

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ34
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 2: After reading Who were the participants in this study? Do you think this number is large enough to provide reliable data? What does the text tell you about these participant? What other information would you like to know about them? Was this research quantitative or qualitative? What are the advantages of the type of the research chosen? What are the disadvantage? This research was carried out in the US. To what extent are these results generalizable to other part of the world?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ12.2
constructive_questions.Details: How should university lecturers integrate social media into their classroom? Justify your position.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ35
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 3: Before reading Do you think Facebook can be used as a learning tool? Why or why not? To what extent should university and college professors incorporate social media into their instruction? Explain your opinion.

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ12.3
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 3:How well do your personal experiences align with the author's conclusion?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ36
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 3: After reading Why did the author decide to carry out this study? Describe the author's research methodology. Would you have done anyting differently? Why? The author recognizes that the number of participants in the study is "very small". What do you think would be an optimal number of participants in this type of study? If you have used social media tools for educational purposes, how do the author's conclusions compare with your own experiences? What is the purpose of the author's statement in the "Conclusions" section that "the findings cannot be generalized" (line 254)? Why not? What do you think future research by this author could focus on? Would you personally like to use Facebook in your academic studie, or do you prefer to keep Facebook for personal use only? Explain your answer.

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ13.1
constructive_questions.Details: How significant are the anecdotes, visuals, figures, and quotations utilised in the text as evidence?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ37
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 1 Do an Internet search about "feng shui". Share your information with your group. "If you change your living and studying space in some way, you will experience improvements in your life". Do you agree or disagree with this idea?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ13.2
constructive_questions.Details: Do Internet search about FENGSHUI. How have the principles of this art been incorporated into your culture?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ13.3
constructive_questions.Details: Discuss the benefits and drawbacks of utilising a treadmill desk using information from the reading and your personal experiences.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ39
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 2: before reading Have you ever suffered any negative effects from sitting too long? What workspace features would you recommend in order to improve health and productivity? Do an Internet search for pictures of treadmill desks. What advantages and disadvantages do you think these desks might have?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ14.1
constructive_questions.Details: What types of evidence are employed in Reading 2? How effective are they? Explain.

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ14.2
constructive_questions.Details: Do you prefer working in a traditional or open-plan office? Explain your decision.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ41

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ14.3
constructive_questions.Details: How might the workstation design affect employees' productivity? Explain your response using facts and examples from the reading and/or your own knowledge.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ42
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 3: After reading What recommenndation would you make to anyone responible for deigning a new office space? What problems do workers in open-plan office have? How might these problems be addressed?

constructive_questions.Details: According to you, what variables impact the happiness of an individual and a nation? Explain

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ43
constructive_questions.Details: Why do you think some countries are much richer than others? What are some contributing factors to the relative wealth of a country? What are the three most important in determining the happiness of a country? Why do you think so?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ15.2
constructive_questions.Details: Based on the information provided in Reading 1, what recommendations would you make to the Vietnamese government and to your friends?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ44
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 1: After reading Explain in your own words the meaning of "diminishing marginal return". Give some examples. To what extent should governments make economic policies based on this kind of research Why? Based on the information in this article, what recommendations would you personally make to the government of Vietnam and your friends and family?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ15.3
constructive_questions.Details: How much do you agree with the United Nations' six factors for a happy nation? Explain.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ45
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 2: Before reading What do you know about the country of Denmark? It is stated that Denmark is the happiest country in the world. What do you think are the reasons? Explain. Is it realistic to measure the happiness of various countries? What factors do you think should be considered when trying to do so? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ16.1
constructive_questions.Details: What characteristics do the 10 happiest nations (Denmark, Norway, Switzerland, Netherland, Sweden, Canada, Finland, Austria, Iceland, Australia) have in common? Use textual evidence and personal experience to support your response.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ46
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 2: After reading The ten happiest countries are Denmark, Norway, Switzerland, Netherland, Sweden, Canada, Finland, Austria, Iceland, Australia. Which of their common features do you think are related to happinest? Why? What light is shed on the subject of happiness economics by the naming of Denmark as the world's happiest country? Can other countries learn anything from the example of Denmark?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ16.2
constructive_questions.Details: How does the happiness of Bhutan differ from that of Denmark? Explain your response using facts and examples from the two readings and/or your own knowledge.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ47
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 3: Before reading What do you know about Bhutan and its GDP? Do you expect people in Bhutan to be generally happy or unhappy? Why? What might contribute to their happiness or to their lack of happiness?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ16.3
constructive_questions.Details: What could be learned from Bhutan's approach to achieving national success?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ48
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 3: After reading What is your opinion about the four pillars of GNH (Gross National Happiness). Are their any factor that could be added to this list? Why? It could be said that Bhutan has focue on happiness at the expense of investment in roads, electricity and other necessary improvements to the country's infratructure. How do you think a member of Bhutanese government would respond to this? Have the Bhutanese formulated a new approach to measuring successs? What, if anything, could world governments and economists learn from Bhutan's approach o national success?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ17.1
constructive_questions.Details: How has the Internet altered social interaction?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ49
constructive_questions.Details: How is a friend different from an acquaintance, colleague or a classmate? How do you know when someone has become a friend? In what way(s) has the Internet changed the nature of socializing? Do you think these changes are positive or negative?

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ17.2
constructive_questions.Details: To what extent do you agree with the following statement: "In the end, a touch in the real world is worth a thousand words in the virtual world." Explain your answer and include examples from your knowledge and experience

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ50
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 1: After reading "What bonds the community together is a common sense of obligation, reciprocity and trust". To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement? Explain. "The fact that social networks in our urganized world are fragmented and geographically distributed means that there is less to bind us into the baric of our local community. We don't even know most of the people we pass in the street." Do you agree or disagree with this idea? Explain.

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ17.3
constructive_questions.Details: Do you believe that "Dunbar's number" is still relevant these days? Include facts and examples from the reading and/or your own understanding to support your answer.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ51
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 2: Before reading The title of this reading asks: "Is Dunbar's friend-limiting number still relevant in this Facebook era?" What do you predict the answer to this question will be? Why? Describe your own involvement with social media such as Facebook and friends there.

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ18.1
constructive_questions.Details: What have you learned from the experiment conducted by the author?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ52
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 2: After reading Why do you think people add "friends" on social media that they don't know personally? How do you respond to "friend" requests from strangers? Do you think the author's experiment was a waste of time, or do you think it taught him a useful lesson? Explain your answer. Write a response to the following message "I only have fifty-eight friends on Facebook. I feel like a social failure."

constructive_questions.Name: HCM_CQ18.2
constructive_questions.Details: Compare the generation of "digital natives" to prior generations. Explain your response using facts and examples from the reading and/or your own knowledge.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ53
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 3: Before reading What do you understand by the term "digital native"? Do you think you are a digital native? Why, or why not? How is the workplace different for today's graduates than it was for their parent? What work-related skills might digital natives have that their parents' generation does not have?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ54
constructive_questions.Details: Reading 3: after reading The authors say: "…as these 'Generation Y' individuals grow into the managerss and chief executive officers of tomorrow, they will be uniquely placed to take on the challenges of virtual teams (lines 117 to 121). a) If you consider yourself to be a digital native, do you agree that your use of social media has given you an advantage in the workplace? Why or why not? b) If you do not consider yourself to be a digital native, do you feel that you are disadvantged in today's workplace? Why, or why not? Do you think universities and colleges should modify their courses to prepare students better for a career in which they might have to work virtually with people in different parts of the world? If so, in what ways could this happen? If not, why not?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ55
constructive_questions.Details: Should space exploration be prioritized by governments? If so, why? Do an Internet search about the early days of space exploration in the time of the Cold War. What has changed since that time? What has stayed the same? Is there a role for private enterprises in space exploration Why, or why not?

constructive_questions.Details: Reading 1: before reading Have you ever looked up the starts and wondered about life and the universe? What questions have you asked? "Why spend so much money sending satellites into space when people around the world are starving?" How would you answer this question? Can you think of any specific technological items we now have on Earth a a result of space exploration?

What could the human race gain by changing conditions on Mars to make the planet suitable for humans to live there? What might be the drawback of doing this? Would you be interested in travelling to Mars? What kinds of people do you think would be best suited to this endeavour?
